summary: Kazuhiro Furuta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at the Otani Academic Society, attested in 1991, and served as Dean at Otani University, attested in 1998.
Kazuhiro Kaneiwa specializes in Buddhist studies. His career includes posts at Bukkyo University, attested in 2001 and 2013.
Kazuhiro Kawasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral coursework at Koyasan University, where he also held a researcher post around 2004.
Kazuhiro Yamamoto specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Silpakorn University, attested in 2009, completing doctoral work under supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.
Kazumi Yoshizaki works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Yoshizaki studied at Toyo University and held a post at the National Museum of Ethnology, attested in 2001.

Wasō Harada specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku and Koyasan universities under several teachers, he later held posts at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University (1999–2006), and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (2002–2007).

Kazunobu Matsuda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and served as a lecturer there (attested 1985–1988), before holding professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto University.

Kazuo Enoki was a scholar of Central Asian history, Sinology, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1933–1936), later serving there as an assistant professor (~1948–1955) and holding a post at Toyo Bunko (~1941–1989).

Kazuo Hyodo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University, where he earned his doctorate under Hajime Sakurabe, later serving as associate professor (~1983–2014) at Otani University.

Kazuo Kano specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned an MA at Kyoto University and a PhD at the University of Hamburg (2006), later holding posts at Koyasan University and Komazawa University.
Kazuo Matsumura is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1972–1976) and held posts at Tenri University (~1990–1997) and Wako University (~1997–2019).

Kazuo Okabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, later serving as an associate professor (1973) and professor (1979–2006) at Komazawa University.

Kazuo Osumi was a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Hokkaido University (1964) and Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
Kazuo Oyamada specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tamagawa University (~1970–1974) and held a post at Rissho University (~1984–2022).
Kazutoshi Soma works in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied under Meiji Yamada and held a lecturer position at Ryukoku University, attested in 1987.

Kazuyoshi Hotta specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Hotta pursued doctoral studies and held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007), later holding an appointment at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and founded Shinnyokai. He served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).
Keenan W. Cox is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Cox completed an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, attested in 2014.
Kees W. Bolle was a scholar of religion, history, and Indology. He studied at Leiden, Madras, and Chicago (PhD under Mircea Eliade), and served as Professor of History at UCLA (~1967–1994).

Kei Kataoka is an Indologist and philosopher educated at the University of Tokyo and Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha. He held positions at the University of Tokyo, Fukuoka University, and Kyushu University.
